title: Ind-etale maps induce separable algebraic residue extensions
statement: Let $f:A\to T$ be an ind-etale homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$, put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. The canonical extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ of residue fields [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. In particular, if $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ are maximal, the canonical map $A/\mathfrak p\to T/\mathfrak q$ is a separable algebraic extension. No finite-type assumption on $T$ is required.
